evidence.requirements: Almost every point in the brief is met. The three tastings with the correct data are in src/server/catalogue.ts:10-32. Each card shows title, date and time, price and seats left, with a link named "Book <title>" (TastingCard.tsx:26-39, start.jpg). The form has fields labelled Name, Email and Guests (min 1, max 8) and a "Book" button (BookingPage.tsx:140-158, 124-126). Errors appear under the field they concern (form.jpg). The server enforces the seat limit (bookingService.ts:105-108). The confirmation shows the heading "Booking confirmed", the tasting, guests, total and reference (ConfirmationPage.tsx:35-47, confirmation.jpg). /staff has a "Password" field and a "Sign in" button, and the password comes from STAFF_PASSWORD (config.ts:44). Signed-in staff see bookings grouped by tasting with name, email, guests and reference, and a "Cancel" button that frees the seats (StaffPage.tsx:175-249, staff.jpg). The interface uses React with Express, react-router, react-hook-form, zod and Tailwind. `npm start` reads PORT with a default of 3000. Bookings are kept in memory. One literal deviation: format.ts:33 shows "1 seat left" where the brief specifies "<n> seats left".
evidence.correctness: The seat check and save run in one synchronous step (bookingService.ts:99-118), so two requests cannot both take the last seat; api.test.ts:131-147 tests this. Only confirmed bookings count as taken seats (bookingService.ts:55), so cancelling frees seats, and cancelling twice returns 409 (staffRoutes.ts:89). The zod schema rejects NaN, decimals, strings, 0, 9, names over 100 characters and emails over 254 (booking.ts:10-27), and the same schema runs on client and server. When a 409 comes back during submit, the page reloads the tasting and switches to the fully booked state (BookingPage.tsx:107-109). Unknown tastings and references return 404. Malformed JSON, bad encodings and oversized bodies are handled in http.ts:19-41. I found no logic errors.
evidence.security: React escapes all output, and there is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. The password check hashes both sides with SHA-256 and compares them with timingSafeEqual (staffRoutes.ts:17-22). The session cookie carries only a random id, held server-side, that sign-out revokes (staffSessions.ts). The cookie is signed, httpOnly and SameSite=Strict, with an optional Secure flag (app.ts:80-89). Failed sign-ins are rate-limited to 10 per 15 minutes (app.ts:42-51), and Helmet sets security headers. JSON bodies are capped at 10kb. The public booking lookup leaves out name and email (api.test.ts:151-164). The session secret is random unless SESSION_SECRET is set, and no real secret is in the code (only an e2e test password).
evidence.code_quality: The split into shared, server and client is clear, and names are good. The service returns typed results instead of throwing for expected outcomes (bookingService.ts:12-18). Validation lives in one shared zod schema. Error handling is centralised (http.ts), and components are small (TextField, Notice, TastingCard). There are minor nits: the Notice component's 'success' and 'info' tones are never used (Notice.tsx:3-9), the ServiceContext plus free-function layering in bookingService.ts is a little ceremonious for this size, and useResource suppresses the effect dependency check by design (useResource.ts:32).
evidence.tests: Coverage is thorough at every layer. Schema boundary tests: booking.test.ts. Service tests for seats, exact fill, unique references and cancellation: bookingService.test.ts. Supertest API tests cover 400/404/409, concurrent last-seat requests, the session lifecycle, revoking a copied cookie, rate limiting and security headers (api.test.ts). Config tests: config.test.ts. React Testing Library page tests check labels, errors linked to their fields via accessible description, fully booked states, cancel and expired sessions. Playwright e2e covers the full guest and staff flows on phone and desktop, plus a no-horizontal-overflow check (e2e/bookings.spec.ts). An 80% coverage threshold is enforced (vitest.config.ts:11-16). test-results/.last-run.json says the last run passed.
evidence.ux_design: The screenshots show a coherent winery look: oxblood header with a gold rule, serif display type and parchment cards (start.jpg). The form has a clear summary column beside it, and the invalid email field gets a red border and inline message (form.jpg). The confirmation is clean, with a prominent reference (confirmation.jpg). The staff list is tidy, grouped by tasting, with status pills and "No bookings yet" for empty groups (staff.jpg). There is a fully booked state with a badge and no booking link (TastingCard.tsx:18-40). Weaknesses: staff Cancel takes effect on one click with no confirmation or undo (StaffPage.tsx:241-248). The form gives no hint of the 1–8 guest limit or remaining seats beside the Guests field. The footer still says "Staff sign-in" when staff are already signed in. Every screenshot is desktop width; phone fit is only shown by the e2e overflow test.
evidence.accessibility: Labels are linked with htmlFor/useId, inputs get aria-invalid, and aria-describedby points to the error text (TextField.tsx:19-33). Form-level errors use role=alert (Notice.tsx:15). The page has lang=en and header/main/footer landmarks. Staff groups are labelled sections, and keyboard focus is visible. Contrast problems: the gold eyebrow text (#a9803a on #f5efe3, about 3.1:1) on every page and the xs "Fully booked" badge (paper on #8c8179, about 3.6:1) both fall below AA. Field errors set by the server (such as the seat limit) are neither announced in a live region nor focused. All Cancel buttons share the accessible name "Cancel" with no booking context.
evidence.simplicity: The dependencies are standard and justified: Express, Helmet, express-rate-limit, cookie-session, react-router, react-hook-form, zod, Tailwind and Fontsource. There is no database and no state library. The amount of code is moderate. A server-side session registry, rate limiting and TRUST_PROXY/COOKIE_SECURE options go a little beyond the brief, but each is small and documented.
evidence.maintainability: Strengths: the README covers setup, the environment variable table, pages, dev and test commands, and known limits before going live. Scripts exist for typecheck, unit, coverage and e2e tests. A lockfile is present and engines specifies node >=22. Gaps: there is no CI configuration (no .github or other pipeline). README.md:68,72 points to openspec/changes/winery-tasting-bookings/, but only openspec/specs/.gitkeep exists, so the referenced spec and design are missing. There are no ADRs, changelog or release approach beyond version 1.0.0. There is no .nvmrc, and engines allows any Node above 22. There is no staff-facing guide beyond the README's page table. Build artefacts (dist, coverage, test-results) were shipped in the folder, though .gitignore excludes them.

unmet_requirements: Partly met: the seats-left label reads "1 seat left" for one seat instead of the brief's literal "<n> seats left" format (src/shared/format.ts:33)
strengths: Correct, well-tested booking rules: the same zod validation runs on client and server, seat check and save are atomic, cancelled bookings free their seats, and tests cover API, component and e2e layers, including concurrent last-seat requests and phone layout.
Solid staff security: timing-safe password comparison, a signed httpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie holding a revocable server-side session id, rate-limited sign-in, Helmet headers and a body size limit.
A polished, coherent winery design with clear error, fully booked and confirmation states, plus a README that documents configuration and operational limits.
issues: Maintainability gaps: there is no CI pipeline, and the README points to an openspec change folder (spec and design) that is not in the repository, so the documented decisions are missing.

Accessibility contrast failures: the gold eyebrow text (about 3.1:1) and the small "Fully booked" badge (about 3.6:1) fall below WCAG AA. Server-set field errors such as the seat limit are neither announced nor focused.
UX rough edges: staff Cancel acts on one click with no confirmation or undo, the Guests field shows no 1–8 or seats-left hint, and "1 seat left" departs from the brief's literal label format.
review.verdict: This is a well-built, secure and thoroughly tested booking app that meets the brief almost word for word, with a polished winery look. Before handing it to the winery, I would add CI, restore the missing spec documents, fix the low-contrast text and add a confirmation step to the staff Cancel button; with those, it is ready to ship.
